research_thread.scientific_problem: Understanding the magnetic origin of phase stability and mechanical response (stacking fault formation) in Cantor alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) at finite temperatures.
research_thread.intervention: First-principles simulation accounting for longitudinal spin fluctuations (LSFs) as a function of temperature and volume.
research_thread.baseline: Standard DFT or models neglecting LSFs, or assuming purely static magnetic states.
research_thread.conditions: Finite temperature (starting 50K), paramagnetic state, fcc and hcp crystal structures.
research_thread.structure: Face-centered cubic (fcc) and hexagonal close-packed (hcp) polymorphs.
research_thread.outcome: LSFs induce sizable magnetic moments in Co, Cr, Ni; hcp is energetically preferred at cryogenic T; negative stacking fault energy at low T, positive at high T; suppression of nano-twins at high T.
research_thread.mechanism: Longitudinal spin fluctuations generate temperature-dependent magnetic moments that alter the magnetic entropy contribution to free energy, shifting the stability balance between fcc and hcp phases.

evidence_spans: Here we use first-principles alloy theory to investigate the magnetic structure of polymorphic CoCrFeMnNi in the paramagnetic state by accounting for the longitudinal spin fluctuations (LSFs) as a function of temperature.
In both face-centered cubic (fcc) and hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structures, the LSFs induce sizable magnetic moments for Co, Cr and Ni.
The impact of LSFs is demonstrated on the phase stability, stacking fault energy and the fcc-hcp interfacial energy.
The hcp phase is energetically preferable to the fcc one at cryogenic temperatures, which results in negative stacking fault energy at these conditions.
With increasing temperature, the stacking fault energy increases, suppressing the formation of stacking faults and nano-twins.

Accounting for the LSFs at finite temperature (contour plots in Fig. 1 ), finite magnetic moments have been thermally induced for Cr, Ni and Co at all volumes even at the lowest temperature considered here (50 K) in both the fcc and hcp phases.
High pressure synthesis of a hexagonal close-packed phase of the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi.
